note: M5: one photoreal keyframe per B→V shot, made with FLUX.2 [dev] from the shot's Blender first frame (reference image 1: layout, renders/m5/plates/<shot>/) and the reference sheets (images 2+). V animates from it, guided by the same plate's depth, so the keyframe keeps the layout's geometry: the sampler starts from the layout at partial denoise. Text is the overlays': signs, screens and the billboard stay plain. Act 2 is the same night as Act 1, now in rain (brief, S42). S43 v2: v1 (denoise 0.92) kept the stand-in's cartoon head and eyes; v2 starts from noise (denoise 1.0) with the layout as a reference only, and asks for natural proportions. S43 v3 (2026-11-01, the human's note): v2 put a payphone on the wall; v3 adds the set's payphone (a crop of S42's layout) as reference image 3 and places it at the frame's right edge, as in the layout. v4 (2026-11-01, the human: "still reading more like Queens than it is Tenderloin"): red brick walk-ups, a long flat street and orange sodium light read as New York. The "tenderloin" sentence (pale stucco and terracotta apartment hotels with cornices, bay windows and fire escapes, blade signs, scissor gates, trolley-bus wires, a hill) goes in every street shot's prompt, and the light is San Francisco's white LED streetlights.
layout_prefix: Reference image 1 is a rough 3D layout of this exact shot. Keep its camera angle, lens, framing, horizon line and perspective exactly, and keep every building, object and figure in the same place and pose. Turn the stand-in shapes into the real, photographed things described below, as a still from a high-budget cinematic film.
style: Night, steady light rain, wet surfaces, cinematic 35mm film look, shallow depth of field, cool white LED streetlights and colored neon, deep shadows, natural skin texture. Every sign, screen and label is plain and blank, with no text, letters, numbers or logos.

S43.prompt: A tight close-up of the man from reference image 2, a real adult man with natural human proportions, normal-sized eyes and a lean face: the same face, short black curly hair, teal hoodie with white drawstrings and the straps of a tan canvas apron. Reference image 1 gives the camera angle, the framing and where things stand; the cartoon figure in it becomes this real man, head and shoulders filling the frame. He stands on a city street corner at night and looks straight into the camera, lips parted mid-word as he raps, calm and knowing. Raindrops bead on his face and hair. Behind him, softly out of focus: on the left, the old brick corner wall of a shop with a rolled-down corrugated metal shutter; on the right edge of the frame, partly cut off, the old freestanding payphone from reference image 3, a dark blue phone housing on a square metal post standing on the sidewalk, with a glowing white blank sign box on its top; behind it the street, wet asphalt reflecting the lights. {tenderloin}

tenderloin: The street is in San Francisco's Tenderloin: six- and seven-story early-1900s apartment hotels with flat fronts in pale gray, cream and beige painted stucco and terracotta, ornate cornices at the roofline, stacked bay windows, black fire escapes zigzagging down the facades, vertical neon blade signs on the hotels, black scissor security gates and roll-down shutters on the ground-floor shops, a slim gray parking meter, Muni trolley-bus wires strung across the street overhead, and in the distance the street climbs a steep hill.
